REGULAR MEETING OF THE BALDWIN PARK RECREATION AND
  COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF BALDWIN PARK,
  Council Chambers
  Monday, January 4, 2016
  6:00 p.m.

The meeting was Called to Order at 6:00pm, by Commissioner Watkins.

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Chair Person Brito.

ROLL CALL:  Commissioners Avila, Brito, Grijalva, Lujan and Watkins.

ABSENT :  Sal Barrientos and Madeline Gutierrez

ALSO PRESENT: Maria Moreno Program Supervisor, Armando Nava, Program
  Coordinator and Teresa Alexander Commission Secretary

It was moved and seconded to approve the Certificate of Posting for January 4, 2016.
M/S/C: WATKINS/AVILA

It was moved and seconded to approve the Minutes of December 7, 2015.
M/S/C: LUJAN/WATKINS

PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS

NONE.

REGULAR MEETING OF THE BALDWIN PARK  January 4, 2016
RECREATION AND COMMUNITY SERVICES
COMMISSION
 REPORTS OF OFFICERS, COMMISSIONERS OR COMMITTEES

  1. Santa Clothes Program Update

Program Supervisor Maria Moreno gave the Commissioners an update regarding Santa
Clothes Program. Santa Clothes was on Tuesday, December 8, 2015 at Wal-Mart in
Baldwin Park. We were able to give 300 kids a $50 gift card to shop at Wal-Mart each
child was also able to receive a toy, age appropriate. With their $50 gift card, the
students were able to purchase a holiday outfit and in some case a pair of shoes also.

  2. Christmas Food Basket Program Update

Program Coordinator Armando Nava, gave the Commissioners an update regarding the
Christmas Food Basket Program. The Christmas Food Baskets took place on Saturday,
  th
December 12 at the Esther Snyder Community Center. For the past few years the
program has been a drive thru pick. Residents are given a time to pick up their basket.
This is to help insure the crowd is contained. Residents do not have to get up early and
wait in the cold for a spot in line. They are guaranteed a basket. This year we were able
to hand out 380 baskets the day of the event. After all of those were picked up we were
able to call residents on the waiting list and they were able to pick up a basket. Some of
the sponsors for the program were Navidad en el Barrio, Vallarta Markets, Baldwin Park
Unified School District, Baldwin Park Adult & Community Education, D&D Warehouse,
Church of the Redeemer, Baldwin Park Key Club and Sierra Vista Key Club. We
appreciate all of the sponsors and their dedicated support. We would not be able to
have such a successful event each year. We were able to put $60-$70 worth of food in
the baskets. The boxes were really heavy and full, in hope to feed a family of 5 for 3
days. We had fresh produce as well as canned food. We collected over 1,000 canned
goods from the schools in Baldwin Park. We hope that everyone is able to attend next.
We appreciate the Commissioners that did attend. Commissioner Lujian shared her
support and said it was an excellent event that was well organized. Program
Coordinator, Armando Nava shared with the Commission that there were a few glitches
that need to be worked out and one of them being the speed of the cars. Next we want
to speed up the vehicle line. We are going to suggest that resident bring trucks instead
of cars so staff can just load it in the bed of the truck rather than trying to fit it in the
trunk or inside the car. We also want to encourage residents to not bring kids with car
seats or extra family members. The box alone takes up a lot of space. We also have
one master list to keep track of all of the baskets being distributed. It reassures us that
there are not any duplicates.

  3. Introduction to New Commissioner

  Program Supervisor, Maria Moreno introduced Northpark High School Student
  Commissioner Anthony Grijalva. Anthony Grijalva is a student at Northpark High

   School and was appointed by the Council.
  4. 2016 Special Events Calendar

Program Supervisor Maria Moreno handed out a list of Special Events for the 2016
calendar year. A few of the upcoming events for the month of February are Senior
Valentine’s Candlelight Dinner and the “State of the City” Address To Be Determined.
The event s that are pending will have an definite date as it gets closer.

  5. Walnut Creek Nature Park Update

Program Supervisor, Maria Moreno gave the Commissioners an update regarding the
Walnut Creek Nature Park Update. Today (Monday, January 4th, 2016 was the officially
start of phase one. They will hopefully be moving quickly with El Nino coming in. Phase
I will be funding of $220,000 Natural Resource Agency and LA County Open Space
$200,000. The District is $420,000. Phase I will include Clearing, grading and grubbing
(prep work), Concrete Walking Path (10’) Part 1 of 2 Solar Lighting Safety and Parking
Lot, Restore Educational Signs at ( Observation Structure Area), Enlarge bioswale and
part 1 of 3 irrigation (rain sense controllers) and landscaping (drought tolerant). The
  st
expected completion date for phase I is March 31 , 2016. Phase II will be funding of
$480,000 Land and Water Conservation Fund and $308,446 LA County Open Space
District. Direct $788,446. Phase II will include Clearing, grading and grubbing (prep
work) ADA Compliance Bridge, Playground Structures, Observation Structure (hand
railings, flooring, fascia boards, roof, paint restrooms. Commissioner Watkins and
Grijalva asked if the restrooms would be handicap accessible. Program Supervisor
Maria Moreno shared that they currently are. Commissioner Watkins informed the
commission that the toilets are not handicap accessible. Program Supervisor, Maria
Moreno informed the Commissioner that she will double check them. We also
submitted a grant today (1/4/16) for Phase III, funding $723,100 from Rivers and
Mountains Conservancy. Phase III will hopefully include the Installation of Security
Cameras, Part 2 solar lighting (walkway and parking lot), Update and repair of the
automatic security gate at Hensel Street, Pedestrian ADA compliant entrance to the
park, Completion of irrigation and drought tolerant landscaping, Completed trail with
PCC and trail Markers. Widened curb inlet (expanding to 24 inches) to park for water
harvesting to bioswale to capture more drained water. Parking lot improvements will
include additional ADA compliant parking stalls, Nature play equipment (natural
activities that will fit with the theme of the park), Installation of monument entrance
signs and addressing natural history, culture history and watershed components. This
grant would fund two additional educational signs to cover additional material. Part 3 of
3 Irrigation (rain sense controllers) and Landscaping (drought tolerant). Walnut Creek is
officially closed during construction starting today (1/4/16). Phase II should start in May
maybe April. We will not hear anything about Phase III for 6 months. We could start in
fall with Phase III. Commissioner Watkins would like a tour during the construction.
Commissioner Grijalva asked about the homeless that often stay at the park. Program

 Supervisor Maria Moreno shared that this positive movement will keep the homeless
out. We will be updating the Commission with pictures. The City of Baldwin Park will be
hosting a Community input meeting at the Esther Snyder Community Center on
January 13th and all Commissioners are encouraged to attend.

Commission Requests and Communications
All the Commission would like to send their condolences to the Mayor for the passing of
his father. All of the Commissioners would like to be notified.

Commissioner Grijalva asked about the Senior Prom. The Senior Prom is a big event in
the Senior Center and we encourage everyone to attend.

Commissioner Lujan wanted to wish everyone a Happy New Year and thank you for the
hard work.

Commissioner Watkins wanted to wish everyone a Happy New Year and thank you for
all of you hard would and the excellent staff.

ADJOURNMENT

With no other business being presented, it was motioned and seconded to adjourn the
